title: Ising antiferromagnet on the snub 24-cell
statement: The snub 24-cell (a uniform 4-polytope found by Gosset, with 96 vertices, 432 edges, 480 triangles and 9 edges at each vertex) is obtained from the 600-cell by removing the 24 vertices of an inscribed 24-cell. Put an Ising spin s_v = +1 or -1 on each vertex and couple the ends of every edge antiferromagnetically: E(s) = sum over the 432 edges uv of s_u s_v. Determine the ground-state energy min E(s) (equivalently the maximum cut of the graph). Known: -158 <= min E <= -144; find a configuration with energy below -144, or prove that -144 is optimal.
submission: Text file: the 96 spins as a string of + and - (or 96 integers 1 and -1) in the checker's vertex order: the 600-cell's vertices with irrational coordinates, in sorted order (see polytope_graph in checkers/orig_phys.py).
score: the energy E(s), an integer (smaller is better)

best_known.source: Quantavane (Arhan Canli), 9 November 2026: a configuration with 144 frustrated edges found by simulated annealing (tools/src/ising.c; three seeds of 30 restarts each reach -144)

context: Frustrated antiferromagnets on polyhedral clusters (the icosahedron, the dodecahedron, the icosidodecahedron and the fullerenes) are a standard testing ground for geometric frustration in magnetic molecules, and the 4-dimensional polytopes are their curved-space relatives (Nelson's icosahedral order lives on the 600-cell; see the problems polytope-ising and potts3-600). The snub 24-cell sits between the 600-cell and the 24-cell: removing an inscribed 24-cell leaves 24 icosahedral and 120 tetrahedral cells, edges lying in 3 or 4 triangles, and a spectrum (smallest eigenvalue 3.29... below zero) that bounds the maximum cut at 295. The best configuration we found has 144 frustrated edges against the eigenvalue bound of 137; the 120-cell, the E8 polytope 4_21 and the Gosset polytope 3_21 are solved exactly by their bounds, so the snub 24-cell and the 600-cell are the open cases we know.
references: T. Gosset, On the regular and semi-regular figures in space of n dimensions, Messenger of Mathematics 29 (1900) 43-48
H. S. M. Coxeter, Regular Polytopes (Dover, 1973)
Snub 24-cell derived from the Coxeter-Weyl group W(D4), arXiv:1106.3433
B. Mohar, S. Poljak, Eigenvalues and the max-cut problem, Czechoslovak Math. J. 40 (1990) 343-352

novelty.verdict: new. The snub 24-cell appears on arXiv only in papers on its symmetry and construction (arXiv:1106.3433, 0906.2109); no spin model, maximum cut or Ising ground state on it was found.
closest: Papers on the snub 24-cell's construction from W(D4) and the E8 root system (arXiv:1106.3433, arXiv:0906.2109): geometry, not spin systems.

rows: exact: our configuration meets the eigenvalue bound (smallest eigenvalue -3)

baseline.text: -144 (144 frustrated edges), held by Quantavane (Arhan Canli), 9 November 2026: the configuration in `refs/snub24-ising.txt`. Lower bound -158 from the eigenvalue bound: max cut <= 96 (9 + 3.2915...) / 4 < 295.

bound.source: eigenvalue bound for the maximum cut, n (k - lambda_min) / 4 = 96 (9 + 3.2915...) / 4 < 295
